learning_signal: A causal chain is complete only when the cause of the cause is a mechanism, and depth is verified by the recurrence test: 'would this failure reappear after my fix?' A fix that does not remove the generative mechanism is a symptom patch even when it looks structural; 'X was never applied' is a fact, not a root. The routed m013 pass contract (5-whys with per-link evidence, fault-tree structure, prevention-vs-detection gap separation) plus a divergence check against a practiced routine (apply-and-check) is what converts the correct-but-shallow diagnosis from 3/5 to 5/5.
suggested_improvement: Keep m013 first-class on diagnose/guarantee incident signatures with the m003 inversion gate; make the recurrence test explicit in the packet's verification plan (fresh-build check incl. a deliberately colliding migration) so the prevention-vs-detection gap separation is executed, not just named; retain the dual-route re-drill of the naive stopping chunk as the divergence check that catches shallow roots.

key_gap: vs baseline: the human baseline is the style's trap executed — the chain is verified to the deepest evidence-supported cause (vendor release process) and made the primary fix (6–8 weeks) while labeling the 30-minute boundary fix (validation + dead-letter + alert) that fully contains the silent loss 'interim'. The v6 route did not route to pure RCA: the KB's negative-case lesson routes deadline data-loss signatures to m044 (stakeholder lens) with the mandatory m019 adversary gate and tempo mode — finance's stale dashboard is the realized harm, so the boundary fix is primary by construction, the 6-day backlog is replayed, and the vendor tail becomes one scoped ticket.
learning_signal: The negative-case fix is routing, not more digging: a verified causal chain that exits authority/budget/timeline is an escalation boundary, not a fix target; the cheap lever that fully closes the harm is the primary fix, and calling it 'interim' is a status error. Routing deadline data-loss incidents to a stakeholder lens (who needs what by when — finance needs the dashboard current, not a vendor renegotiation) makes containment-primary structural, and the adversarial baseline-risk line (inaction = realized 0.4%/night) is what stops the 'wait for the root' posture.
suggested_improvement: Keep the m044-first route on deadline/adversarial data-integrity signatures with the m019 adversary gate (baseline-risk comparison mandatory) and tempo-mode commit at DO; require an inaction-cost sentence and an explicit 'deepest ≠ actionable' line in every such packet; hold the NEG split by ensuring pure-RCA never routes first on these signatures.
